reasons.specificity: It distinctly tracks the shift from the 2001 Marx–Schumpeter myth-cycle account to the 2022 Luhmann–Hayek framework of unbounded markets and social self-description.
reasons.anchoring: The principal quotations occur in the named texts and generally warrant the claims about money as cipher, growth, religious limits, conclusions, and the absence of a declared intertextual revision.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes continuity of conclusions from changes in explanatory support, and separates temporal limits on capitalist myths from substantive limits on capitalism’s religious reach.
reasons.coherence: Attribution and publication order remain consistent, though calling the Abrahamic focus an uncomplicated scope contraction and classifying the later three-step procedure as a claimed relation slightly overstate what those passages establish.
reasons.usefulness: The relation and support tables directly answer the requested inventory and foreground consequential continuity, but extensive repeated scope audits and CHECK metadata reduce desk usability.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Claims are notably bounded and the analysis repeatedly avoids inventing an explicit revision, with only minor inferential overreach in describing the changed religious comparator as a definite narrowing of the earlier position.

score.one_line: A strongly sourced and expert continuity-with-changed-support reading, slightly weakened by overlong audit apparatus and a modest overstatement of scope contraction.
